title: Persistent semantic state population scaling
question: How does learned semantic state-address recall change as the number of opaque persistent state items increases, under a fixed task and learner?
hypothesis: H_scale: learned semantic addressing retains a measurable advantage over a frozen no-learning control as the persistent state pool grows, while addressing cost grows with the scanned pool.

arms.name: analytic
arms.intervention: identity embeddings as exact state-addressing witness

arms.name: no_learning
arms.intervention: same random initialization with no parameter updates

endpoints.name: state_top1_recall
endpoints.role: primary — correct opaque state address selected

endpoints.name: mean_target_state_rank
endpoints.role: secondary — rank of the target state item

endpoints.name: training_successes
endpoints.role: audit — verified positive selections during training

decision_rule.condition: learned state_top1_recall exceeds no_learning at a registered M level
decision_rule.licenses: bounded evidence that the learned state addressor exploits semantic state content at that population size

decision_rule.condition: learned state_top1_recall fails to exceed no_learning throughout the registered M levels
decision_rule.licenses: the registered learner does not demonstrate scalable semantic state addressing under this protocol

held_constant: same five-bit semantic signature task as REP-006
same exact one-boundary temporal write/read delay
same 5->8 bilinear addressor and learning rule
same 8 downstream candidate programs and exact structural matcher
addressing scans all M state items; no learned index is introduced
C5 and prior REP evidence remain frozen
